# Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL in Large Language Models

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#confidence-llms)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.14056v1) · arXiv:2508.14056v1 author manuscript, 16 pages including supplement; AAAI 2026 bibliographic record independently matched

**Reading coverage:** Entire manuscript and supplementary prompts, Tables 1-4, examples and figure captions; rendered Table 1/Figure 3 inspected. Publisher endpoint returned non-PDF content, so published-version differences were not established.

## Research question

SQL users need estimates of candidate correctness without knowing the reference query, especially when model internals are restricted.

## Method

Compares verbal self-report, repeated-generation agreement by execution/embedding/schema, and token-probability aggregation. SQL-Aware Confidence filters or folds syntactic alternatives and emphasizes meaningful SQL tokens; execution feedback supplies another signal.

## Evaluation

Spider and BIRD development queries, multiple proprietary and open-weight generators, AUROC and expected calibration error. Ablations vary aggregation, SQL-specific normalization and execution grounding; appendix supplies prompts and case analyses.

## What the results support

SAC-Product leads on Spider and SAC-Average on BIRD in the reported table. Execution consistency is strongest among tested black-box approaches, with extra sampling/execution cost. Performance depends on query length and schema-token composition.

## Limits and qualifications

The favorable aggregation differs by benchmark. Result agreement on a database and confidence normalization do not prove semantic equivalence or identify ambiguous intent. Some experimental descriptions and supplemental model inventories differ; exact snapshots, execution-grounding implementation and significance procedures need more detail for reproduction.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A source of candidate-confidence baselines and cost/access trade-offs for abstention pipelines; it does not itself evaluate an ambiguity-resolution dialogue.
